sentences.text: The Kingdom of Ayutthaya -LRB- -LSB- ɑːˈjuːtəjə -RSB- อยุธยา , -LSB- ʔajúttʰajaː -RSB- ; also spelled Ayudhya or Ayodhaya -RRB- was a Siamese kingdom that existed from 1351 to 1767 .	Ayutthaya	Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya (city)	Siamese	Thailand

Ayutthaya was friendly towards foreign traders , including the Chinese , Vietnamese , Indians , Japanese and Persians , and later the Portuguese , Spaniards , Dutch , English and French , permitting them to set up villages outside the walls of the capital , also called Ayutthaya .	Ayutthaya	Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya (city)	Chinese	Chinese people	Vietnamese	Vietnamese people	Indians	Indo-Aryan peoples	Japanese	Japanese people	Persians	Persian people	Portuguese	Portuguese people	Spaniards	Spaniards	Dutch	Dutch people	English	English people	French	French people
In the sixteenth century , it was described by foreign traders as one of the biggest and wealthiest cities in the East .

The court of King Narai -LRB- 1656 -- 88 -RRB- had strong links with that of King Louis XIV of France , whose ambassadors compared the city in size and wealth to Paris .	King	Ayutthaya Kingdom#Kings of Ayutthaya	Narai	Narai	Louis XIV of France	Louis XIV of France

By 1550 , the kingdom 's vassals included some city-states in the Malay Peninsula , Sukhothai , Lan Na and parts of Burma and Cambodia .	Sukhothai	Sukhothai Kingdom	Malay Peninsula	Malay Peninsula	Lan Na	Lan Na	Burma	Burma	Cambodia	Cambodia
This part of the Kingdom 's history is sometimes referred to as ` The Ayutthayan Empire . '

In foreign accounts , Ayutthaya was called Siam , but many sources say the people of Ayutthaya called themselves Tai , and their kingdom Krung Tai `` The Tai country '' .	Ayutthaya	Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya (city)	Tai	Tai peoples
It was also referred to as Iudea in a painting that was requested by the Dutch East India Company	Dutch	Dutch people	Dutch East India Company	Dutch East India Company
